paper_title: Searching for Low-Mass Axions using Resonant Upconversion
notes: Paper presents exclusion limits from the UPLOAD (UPconversion Low-Noise Oscillator Axion Detection) experiment, a room-temperature resonant AC haloscope searching for axions via photon upconversion. The experiment excludes axions with masses between 1.12–1.20 μeV (corresponding to frequencies 271.7–290.3 MHz) above a coupling strength of g_agamma = 3×10^-6 GeV^-1 after 30 days of measurement. This represents a three order of magnitude improvement over their previous result. The experiment is also sensitive to the newly proposed g_aBB coupling term (quantum electromagnetodynamical axion coupling), for which the same exclusion limit applies. The mass range is encoded as a horizontal line at the stated coupling value. Standard virialized halo dark matter model assumed with local density ρ_a ≈ 0.3 GeV/cm^3 (typical galactic halo value). Confidence level is 95% as stated in Fig. 7.
